newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - April 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - April 30.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- CO-OP AIMS FOR TESCO LEAGUE IN 200 MILLION STG REVAMP

Co-operative Retail Services yesterday announced a pre-tax loss of 13.9 million stg after restructuring costs of 18 million stg for the year to January 25. The company revealed plans to spend 200 million stg on restructuring over the next 12 months in an attempt to compete with Tesco and Sainsbury and forestall hostile takeover attempts.
-- P&O'S STERLING GIVEN 31 PERCENT SALARY INCREASE

Lord Sterling, chairman of P&O received a 31 percent pay rise last year, up from 587,000 to 771,000 stg, it was revealed yesterday. Other senior figures also received large rises, which the company said reflected the company's financial performance and progress on corporate strategy.
-- POWER GROUPS AWAIT PENSION RULING

A High Court judge will tomorrow decide who is liable for the legal costs of pensions litigation which may cost the electricity companies over one billion stg. National Grid is appealing against an order by the pensions ombudsman that it repay 46 million stg it withdrew from a surplus in its pension scheme. 13 other electricity companies made similar withdrawals.
THE TIMES
-- CARLTON TALKS TO BT ON DIGITAL TV LINK

A group led by Carlton Communications is negotiating with British Telecom to form an alliance to launch digital TV in terrestrial form. BT is attempting to break into the digital broadcasting business, and Carlton and its partners in the British Digital Broadcasting consortium have invited BT to devise ways of making BDB set-top boxes interactive.
-- EURO DISNEY LOSSES GROW AS INTEREST PAYMENTS RISE

Losses at Euro Disney increased in the six months to March 31 after a rise on the interest rates demanded on its 15 billion francs debts. It lost 210 million francs in the period, compared with 169 million in the same time last year.
-- BA SHARES RISE ON USAIR SALE REPORT
British Airways shares rose yesterday due to speculation that the company is close to announcing the sale of its 24.6 percent stake in USAir. Shares rose from 694p to 704p on news of the negotiation.
THE GUARDIAN
-- NEW CHANCELLOR 'SHOULD RESIST INTEREST RISE'

The National Institute for Economic and Social Research has called on the next Chancellor to resist calls from the Bank of England for a rise in interest rates after the election. In its quarterly report, the institute says taxes may have to be increased to fill the gap in public finances.
-- EU'S BANANA REGIME BARRED

The World Trade Organization has ruled that Europe's policy of favouring banana imports from former French and British colonies violates global free trade rules, following a complaint from the United States. The EU favours a quota system to prevent its market being dominated by Latin American fruit, instead of more expensive fruit from the Caribbean.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- NAMES FUME OVER LLOYD'S BUYOUT MOVE

John Charman, deputy chairman of Lloyd's of London, has moved to buy out the hundreds of individual Names on all of his syndicates. Names see the move as further evidence that the market wants to push out the remaining 10,000 individual investors in favour of corporate capital.
-- SENATORS RE-IGNITE TOBACCO ROW

Five Democrat Senators in the United States have called on Attorney-General Janet Reno to file a federal lawsuit against the tobacco industry to recover the cost of paying Medicare and Medicaid for tobacco-related illnesses. So far, 23 state attorney-generals have filed suits against the industry.
-- BT MAKES FURTHER CUT IN NATIONAL CALL COSTS

British Telecom yesterday announced a further 10 percent cut in daytime national call costs, in a further move in the price competition with cable operators. The calls come as a survey endorsed by industry regulator Oftel shows BT behind rivals in terms of customer satisfaction.
